message.content:
This is a costume, which would fall under HTSUS 9505.90 (festive articles) unless it is classified as wearing apparel. Because the costume is made of textile material, this is a known CBP ruling issue. Under Note 1(e) to Chapter 95, the chapter excludes fancy dress of textiles in chapter 61 or 62, and CBP treats a costume as wearing apparel when it is a well-made garment. Rulings on "Roman Empress" costumes of this kind, a dress with armbands and medallions, tend to find the dress is a "carnival costume" of 6307 or apparel of 6104/6204.

If the dress is a sleeveless pullover knit dress, the heading would be 6104.43 (women's dresses of synthetic fibers, knit). If woven, it would be 6204.43.

Costumes of this kind, such as Roman or Greek goddess dresses, are commonly woven polyester satin. The set includes armbands and medallions, which would make it a set of apparel and accessories. Since Chapter 62 Note 3 sets are for suits and ensembles, I'll classify by the dress. The "Roman Empress" ruling (NY) likely picked 9505.90.6000 as a festive article. The Chapter 95 note excludes only "fancy dress of textiles, of chapters 61 and 62" when it is ordinary apparel, but CBP has often held that costumes of non-durable construction, and in particular those with fairly flimsy materials, are festive articles. Since the description gives no fabric and the set includes medallions and armbands, I'll go with the festive classification.
